recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No follow-up is needed for FHIR-31799 unless BRR later decides to remodel packaging materials based on new implementer experience.
issue_request: FHIR-31799 was a Published FHIR-core BRR change request for the R4 MedicinalProductPackaged artifact, applied for R5 with Persuasive with Modification resolution. It asked the specification to clarify what packaging alternateMaterial represents and whether alternate materials can be mixed and matched; the final Jira comments supplied the intended replacement definition.
initial_application: No prior AutoFHIR audit commit for FHIR-31799 was present on the combined branch. Source history shows commit 8f276af029 applied "improved alternate material definition FHIR#31799" to PackagedProductDefinition.package.alternateMaterial, and c582702619 synced the same wording from R4B. Later resource/path refactors preserved the wording at the current PackagedProductDefinition.packaging.alternateMaterial path.
additional_context: The current build has PackagedProductDefinition as an active resource in source/fhir.ini, while the old MedicinalProductPackaged name is a redirect. The current source definition exactly carries the Jira-approved wording, including the example of different types of plastic for a blister sleeve. Direct Zulip and Confluence searches found no community record that conflicts with the Jira/source conclusion.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current authoritative source already explains alternateMaterial as an allowed substitute for the usual material for that packaging part, so adding or changing text would be redundant and could drift from the applied WG wording.
